steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Seems like you've already made up your mind.
You nod.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: First, we need to go into the mine again. We have to try harder to break through the contamination layer blocking the path and destroy the dead half of the Corpus. Then, we'll go exterminate the living half that has been exposed.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Mmm... this plan remains unchanged.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: But I won't use any help from Rustfire.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm going to get the FAC to break through the contamination layer and remove the dead Corpus from the bottom.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The target is clear, and we don't need that many people. They'd agree to it.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: ...As soon as the FAC enters Inner Bay, everything about us will be exposed. They will take over BR-002. You want to betray Rustfire.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: This is to protect everyone's lives.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You want to dash everyone's hopes, reveal our secrets, and extinguish our one last dream...

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Ha... History really does repeat itself.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You think I'd let an ugly plot twist stain my poem twice?
Her ink condenses, and something lands on your shoulder. One raven, two ravens... Jet-black feathers fall off their bodies. Raven stares at you coldly from behind.
You take a deep breath.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: If you don't agree, there is still the second option.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I will leave this place to find the escaped half of the Corpus.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Take your time... By the time you find it, the Executive Committee would have razed the Drifter Camp to the ground.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: No, I can buy more time for Rustfire.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I already have a lot of information about BR-002. I will use any means necessary to get the Executive Committee to stop the Black Ring. I'll make them drop everything else they're doing to focus on tracking down the living half of the Corpus.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Since the incidents in Eastside were able to contain the FAC, it shows that the City Council cares more about "those incidents" than all of West District. Let's just fool them, then.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We'll use the intelligence to tell them a story. We'll say that what happened in Eastside is closely linked to BR-002. Let's use... the abnormal fluctuations of the major black rings and our "old friend" Parma. Both are quite "mysterious" anyways.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: <size=29>In short, we'll scare the councilors into thinking that they can't stop the troubles in Eastside without resolving the Corpus of BR-002 first. Since the FAC can't leave Eastside right now, we'll ask the Executive Committee to drop what they're doing and help us with West District.</size>

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If I get the chance, I'll also bring Rustfire into the mix. "The Drifter Camp has gained ample battle experience after dealing with the Corpus of BR-002." That way, you'll have more time and an extra layer of protection.
Since you walked through that door, this is the first time Raven has shown some enthusiasm.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: ...Pretty creative. What are the odds of succeeding?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Comparing it to your suicide plan?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Both are quite slim. So why not try a safer approach?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: ...Hahahahahaha!

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Sorry, I just remembered someone accusing Rustfire of being stubborn and knowing only how to be cannon fodder. So it would seem like she has a point.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: I'll join in, and also speed things up.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: I don't want that monster wandering out there for too long. I have a pretty good idea.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: If the apparitions at the bottom of the pit are contamination caused by the living Corpus devouring humans from outside, then the people it devoured might also appear as apparitions at the bottom, near the center.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: While humans cannot penetrate the contamination, my ink can. This star journalist here can help you ask around where the living half of the Corpus is. What do you think?
She surprises you with her frankness.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Not only do I agree, I also want to help you sell this plan.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Haha, but I have to ask my friend first. He calls the shots.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Julien, did you hear what ${PlayerName} said? Do you accept?
She lifts up her hand. A jet-black raven lands on it, tilting its head.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Even though communications are cut off in Inner Bay, I can use my ink raven for long-distance communication. You two leaders can mobilize together.
You realize that Julien is on the other end of the raven. After a brief silence, you decide to speak anyway...

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I'm glad you are still alive.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: If I die, can you stay behind?

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Ha... No? Forget it, then.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: If this continues, Rustfire will only destroy themselves.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Contamination from BR-002 continues to increase, which shows that the other half of the Corpus is highly active. This has already exceeded your expectations.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've checked the Hypercube reserves in the shelter. Even if you all sacrifice your lives, it won't be enough to penetrate the layer. You should all know that, yet no one is stopping.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Because they believe in you. You're their hope.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Be rational. No one there can break through the barrier. If you keep clinging on to this so-called "hope" and making suicidal sacrifices, you'll end up ruining yourselves.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's not hope that's propelling Rustfire anymore. Now you're just doing insane things to run away from despair.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Hope is something precious. It holds a lot of power even when it's irrational.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Eight years ago, when BR-002 broke out, Rustfire didn't give up. They picked up the pieces, supported each other, and clutched onto hope while battling grief, gangsters and Mania.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: We had a leader back then, too.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: He was very strong and brave. Everyone trusted and depended on him. When he disappeared into BR-002, everyone believed he would come back. This faith was what made everyone persevere and keep going.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: But he never came back. He betrayed Rustfire and defected to Nirvana.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: After that, within a week, some fled, some joined gangs, while others simply gave up their lives. Many turned into Corruptors. Rustfire was left in shambles.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: BR-002 didn't kill Inner Bay. He did.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Now, eight years later, many will also consider you the enemy if they see you with the Executive Committee. They will never be able to accept the Executive Committee, nor understand your choice.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: For them, it would be losing their leader and hope all over again.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: But I was never your leader.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Yeah...You're right.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Try it out, Julien. At least this is a realistic hope. Try... and see how it goes.
You want to say something else, but Raven gently covers your mouth. She waves, and the raven dissolves back into her bottle as ink.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Leave the rest to me.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Though he looks aged and hasn't forgotten what happened eight years ago, our architect has a pretty "young" mentality, especially after meeting you.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Did I remind him of something?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You make him remember a lot of things, but we have to look forward. No one will make things hard for you. I'll get someone to escort you out of Inner Bay, and let you know right away if we find any clues about the Corpseborne's other half.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: But I have one condition. Leave your two little pals to me.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Let's see... how about I keep them as hostages! With these two cuties around, I can fool the others, and also deter you from betraying Rustfire. After all, you've never ventured far from them.
She grins and pats you on the shoulder. Her voice becomes gentle once more.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You probably already know that the battlefield you're heading to is far too cruel for them. They won't be able to handle it. You should've done this a long time ago.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Especially that girl. She cares about you too much. It'll kill her.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: To make things fair, I'll let you keep something of mine as hostage, too. Here's my most beautiful and precious poetry book.
She really fetches her poetry book.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: When things calm down, I'll find the chance to send them back to the Bureau. You can cast your shackles on me if you don't believe me. I have to go deep into the contaminated mine anyways. That way, I'll have your protection.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm surprised that you'd really help me.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I thought you'd prefer the original plan. After all, it's more in line with your... dark aesthetic?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Oh, you must've misunderstood. I like those struggling in the darkness because they always hold onto a spark of light. That light is stronger than anything else in the world.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: That spark of light is what makes the darkness meaningful.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: That's why I also like your version of <color=#fb9259>hope</color>.
There's not much to pack. As you leave the room and close the door, the shadow beneath your feet quivers.
After a brief silence, a voice emerges from the shadows.

steps.speaker: Voice in the Shadows
steps.content: You won't be able to catch me, Minos Chief. Don't even think about it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll think about capturing you later. Right now, I have a favor to ask you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: As the guardian of children, I want to ask you to protect those two.

steps.speaker: Voice in the Shadows
steps.content: ...Why don't you do it yourself?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm unable to do that myself right now. I'd only lead them to danger. So, please look after them for me.
Hecate opens her eyes groggily. It's hard to tell the time in the windowless shelter, but she feels like she had slept for a long time and had a long dream.
Hella is still kicking the covers with her feet. Hecate also notices a couple of extra blankets on her body that weren't there last night.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...Chief?
